stem: A research assistant agent attaches the retrieved web page behind each factual statement it makes. Which TWO benefits does this kind of grounding provide? (Select TWO)

options.text: It guarantees that every cited statement is correct
If a statement later proves wrong, reviewers can tell whether the cited page was wrong or the model misreported it
It removes any need to re-check the cited sources as they age
It prevents hallucination everywhere in the answer, including in uncited statements
Readers can verify a claim directly against its source instead of taking the model's word for it

explanation.why_correct: Attaching the retrieved source gives each claim a traceable origin. If an error surfaces, reviewers can check whether the page itself was wrong or whether the model misreported a correct page, and readers can verify the claim against the evidence instead of trusting the model's word.

why_incorrect.A: Grounding does not guarantee correctness, because the retrieved source can itself be outdated, wrong, or misread. It adds traceability, not certainty.
why_incorrect.C: Sources can still go stale or be found questionable, so they may need re-checking. A citation does not retire that need.
why_incorrect.D: Grounding applies to the claims it is attached to. It does not stop the model from hallucinating in statements that carry no source.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Grounding buys traceability and checkability, not a guarantee of correctness.

stem: A task asks the model to explain, in general terms, why the sky appears blue -- a well-established, stable scientific fact. Should the agent invoke an external tool for this?

options.text: Likely not, since this is stable, well-established knowledge that doesn't require current data or a real-world action
Yes, every single response must always use at least one tool call regardless of content
Yes, because the sky's color could have changed since the model's training
It is impossible to answer this question without a tool

explanation.why_correct: Since this is stable, well-established scientific knowledge with no dependency on current, changing data or any real-world action, a tool call is unnecessary and would add latency without a meaningful benefit.

why_incorrect.B: Mandating a tool call for every response regardless of content would waste resources on tasks that are already well within the model's reliable, stable knowledge.
why_incorrect.C: The physical phenomenon causing the sky's blue appearance (light scattering) is a stable, unchanging physical fact, not something that could have 'changed' since training.
why_incorrect.D: This well-established scientific explanation is well within what a model can reliably explain from training alone; a tool is not required to answer it.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Stable, well-established facts with no current-data or action dependency generally don't need a tool call -- reserve tools for genuinely tool-requiring needs.

stem: After a model requests a tool call, who or what actually performs the underlying action and returns a result?

options.text: No execution ever actually occurs; it is purely symbolic
The model directly executes the action within its own text-generation process
A separate execution layer outside the model itself carries out the action and returns the result as an observation
The user must always manually perform the action themselves with no system involvement

explanation.why_correct: The model only requests an action via a tool call; a separate execution layer (outside the model's own text generation) is what actually carries out the action and returns a result, which the model then incorporates as an observation.

why_incorrect.B: The model has no native mechanism to directly execute external actions as part of generating text; it can only request that an action be taken.
why_incorrect.D: Well-designed agentic systems automate tool execution; requiring manual user execution for every tool call would defeat much of the purpose of an autonomous agent.
why_incorrect.A: Real tool calls do trigger actual execution with real effects or data retrieval; it is not merely symbolic or inert.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: The model requests actions via tool calls; a separate execution layer performs them and returns results as observations back to the model.
